common_name: Compacta Strawberry Tree (Dwarf Mediterranean Strawberry Tree)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall in lean, extremely well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Compacta holds a dense, rounded form around 5-6 feet without the pruning the full-size species often needs to stay tidy.

directions: Compacta is a naturally dwarfed selection of the Mediterranean strawberry tree, topping out around 5-6 feet instead of the 15-25 feet the species can reach, which makes it a better fit for foundation plantings, screening, and smaller landscapes where the full-size form would eventually overwhelm the space. It carries the same fall-and-winter overlap of small white urn-shaped flowers and bumpy red-orange fruit as the species, along with the same cinnamon-colored exfoliating bark, just on a more manageable, slower-growing frame. Site it in poor, lean, acidic soil with excellent drainage and avoid rich fertile ground, which pushes soft growth more prone to root and crown disease. Established plants are notably drought-tolerant and rarely bothered by deer, needing only an occasional light shaping cut rather than routine pruning.

common_name: Elfin King Strawberry Tree (Ultra-Dwarf Container Strawberry Tree)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall in lean, extremely well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Elfin King is the most compact named strawberry tree selection and does well as a long-term large-pot specimen as well as in the ground.

directions: Elfin King is an ultra-compact strawberry tree selection, smaller even than the dwarf 'Compacta' form, staying in the 3-5 foot range and well suited to large containers, patios, and tight garden beds where a full-size specimen would not fit. Like its larger relatives it produces the characteristic overlap of small white urn-shaped flowers and rough-textured red-orange fruit in fall and winter, but it tends to flower and set fruit while still young and small rather than needing several years of growth first. Grow it in poor, lean, acidic, sharply drained soil in full sun to light shade; rich garden soil encourages lush, disease-prone growth that works against this selection's naturally tight habit. Once established it tolerates drought well and is rarely troubled by deer, making it a low-maintenance choice for small-space edible landscaping.
